question: what the images, video and iframes of a first view cost in bytes on 16 public sites, what converting each JPEG and PNG to WebP (native size, under a width ceiling, resized to the rendered width, lossless for PNG) would save and at what SSIM, how many image bytes load before the first scroll, and what loading="lazy" removes from that count
instrument: Chromium CDP Network (encodedDataLength, response bodies), DOM image and LCP observations; @gmitch215/tinyimg 1.1.1 for the WebP arms and its milliseconds; SSIM (8 by 8 blocks, luma, both decodes scaled to the converted size, long side at most 512) computed in the page from canvas pixels

method.pages: home plus up to 4 internal pages chosen by payload.ts pickPages from the home page links; the lazy variant visits the first 3 of them
method.context: one fresh browser context per site, profile and variant; both variants route every request through Playwright (the main-frame HTML is fetched by the route and fulfilled, rewritten only in the lazy variant), which turns the browser HTTP cache off, so every page loads with an empty cache; an image row is kept once, on the first page that downloads it
method.scroll: load, wait 1500 ms, record image bytes (before the first scroll), then scroll one viewport at a time up to 40 steps, wait 1000 ms, record again; an image whose request began after the scroll started has phase scroll
method.rendered size: getBoundingClientRect width of the largest showing the URL, after the scroll; CSS backgrounds have none
method.arms: native (WebP quality 80), ceiling (width 2560, fit scale-down, only for files wider than it), resized (width = ceil(rendered CSS width x dpr), only when narrower than the file), lossless (PNG only)
method.ssim: original and converted decoded with createImageBitmap, drawn on white at the converted size scaled so the long side is at most 512, luma, mean SSIM over 8 by 8 blocks
method.lazy: the main-frame HTML is rewritten by rewriteLazy (skip 2) through page.route before the browser sees it; the LCP element is read from a PerformanceObserver before the scroll
method.embeds: a page served at https://spool.test/ holds one iframe to a real YouTube or Vimeo embed, or the facade rewriteEmbeds makes of it; nothing is clicked; 6 s after load; bytes are encodedDataLength of every request except the page
method.request pacing: 250 ms before each page visit, 2 sites at once; the browser fetches a page's own subresources in parallel
